 The Workday Solutions Delivery Manager is accountable end to end for Workday solution delivery, resource management, and operational performance within the HCM Technology portfolio. The role owns execution across Program Increment (PI) delivery, Workday enhancements, AMS oversight, production support, resource capacity and allocation, continuous improvement, and small-to-medium Workday projects.  
 As the primary technology delivery partner for Workday stakeholders, this leader is accountable not only for individual deliverables but also for making sure the right resources and skills are applied to the highest-priority work at the right time. The role combines solution ownership, delivery leadership, service management, and resource management, and remains accountable for outcomes whether work is performed by internal resources or strategic delivery partners.   
 This is an individual-contributor role with no direct reports. The Workday Solutions Delivery Manager leads through influence, clear plans, transparent reporting, and agreed accountability with internal teams, HCM Solution Managers, and delivery partners.  
 Key Responsibilities   
 PI Planning & Delivery   
 Own execution of Workday PI commitments within the assigned solution portfolio.   
 Translate approved business priorities into executable delivery plans and resource requirements.   
 Maintain the Workday delivery backlog so work is refined, estimated, prioritized, and sequenced.   
 Establish achievable PI commitments based on priority, technical dependencies, and available capacity and capability; do not accept commitments without a realistic assessment of both.   
 Coordinate functional, technical, integration, security, testing, and vendor resources required for delivery.   
 Monitor execution against PI commitments and proactively address schedule, scope, dependency, capacity, or quality issues.   
 Provide accurate delivery forecasts and regular reporting on committed versus completed scope, risks, trade-offs, and decisions required.   
 Resource Management, Capacity Planning & Allocation 
This is a core accountability of the role, not an administrative responsibility. The role directs the allocation of Workday delivery capacity without direct people-management responsibility.   
 Own resource planning and allocation across Workday PI delivery, AMS, enhancements, technical debt, and small projects.   
 Maintain an integrated view of Workday demand, available capacity, required skills, committed resources, utilization, and upcoming demand.   
 Allocate internal and partner resources based on business priorities, delivery commitments, operational risk, and required technical and functional skills, in coordination with resource owners.   
 Balance capacity between planned PI delivery and BAU and production-support requirements.   
 Identify capacity constraints, skill gaps, and resource conflicts before they affect delivery commitments; recommend prioritization, sequencing, scope adjustment, or incremental capacity when demand exceeds available resources.   
 Partner with vendors so appropriate functional and technical capabilities are assigned to Workday technical deliverable, and challenge vendor staffing that does not meet agreed skill, quality, or performance expectations.   
 Manage transitions, onboarding, knowledge transfer, and continuity for resources supporting the Workday service.   
 Reduce dependency on individual resources through documentation, cross-training, and succession coverage.   
 Provide resource and capacity forecasts as inputs to HCM portfolio and financial planning, and keep assignments aligned with funded capacity and approved portfolio priorities.   
 Escalate structural capacity or capability gaps with clear recommendations and business impact.   
 Workday AMS & Production Service Ownership   
 Own day-to-day oversight of Workday AMS within the assigned portfolio.   
 Ensure incidents, service requests, defects, and problems are prioritized, assigned, and resolved effectively.   
 Manage ticket backlog, aging, SLA performance, recurring issues, and production risk.   
 Ensure ServiceNow accurately reflects issue status, accountability, and resolution.   
 Require root-cause analysis for significant or recurring incidents, and track corrective actions that address underlying causes through completion.   
 Monitor vendor resource performance, technical and functional quality, continuity, and knowledge coverage.   
 Hold AMS providers accountable for proactive support and continuous improvement.   
 Escalate systemic vendor-performance concerns to the HCM Vendor Operations Lead.   
 Identify recurring failure patterns and lead systemic technical improvements.   
 Enhancement & Small-to-Medium Project Delivery   
 Own Workday enhancements and small-to-medium projects that predominantly reside within the Workday domain.   
 Develop scope, estimates, resource plans, timelines, and delivery approaches.   
 Assign and coordinate appropriate functional, integration, security, testing, and AMS resources.   
 Manage execution through testing, deployment, stabilization, and operational transition.   
 Maintain accountability for the Workday components of larger cross-HCM programs led by Portfolio/Program Management.   
 Ensure project work does not unintentionally compromise PI or critical AMS commitments.   
 Workday Solution Management   
 Maintain strong knowledge of Workday functionality, configuration, integrations, security, and business-process dependencies within the assigned portfolio.   
 Develop strong relationships with HR and Payroll stakeholders and translate business priorities into sustainable Workday solutions.   
 Partner with the HCM Architect on changes involving significant architectural decisions.   
 Maximize standard Workday capabilities and reduce unnecessary customization.   
 Identify technical debt and include appropriate remediation in delivery planning.   
 Assess Workday release impacts and coordinate adoption of relevant new capabilities.   
 Balance immediate business requirements with long-term platform sustainability.   
 Production & Release Readiness   
 Ensure Workday changes follow established development, configuration, testing, security, migration, change, and production-control requirements.   
 Confirm appropriate technical and business testing has been completed and production-readiness criteria are met before deployment.   
 Validate production support, monitoring, deployment, rollback, and stabilization plans.   
 Engage the Technical Delivery Lead for complex, high-risk, or cross-platform releases.   
 Ensure post-production stabilization actions are completed and transitioned into normal operations.   
 Financial & Vendor Stewardship   
 Provide resource demand and capacity inputs into Workday forecasts and annual and ongoing capacity planning.   
 Monitor vendor capacity against funded commitments and planned demand; identify inefficient use of vendor capacity and recommend adjustments.   
 Validate that resource requests are backed by defined demand, outcomes, and appropriate skill requirements.   
 Partner with Vendor Operations on systemic provider-performance issues, contractual service expectations, and resource-model improvements.   
 Stakeholder & Delivery Governance   
 Serve as the primary HCM Technology delivery partner for the assigned Workday portfolio.   
 Give stakeholders clear visibility into commitments, capacity, delivery health, risks, and trade-offs.   
 Facilitate fact-based prioritization when demand exceeds capacity.   
 Resolve issues at the appropriate level, escalating decisions rather than routine execution problems.   
 Coordinate closely with other HCM Solution Managers where Workday work creates downstream dependencies.   
 Decision Rights   
 Although the role has no direct reports, the Workday Solutions Delivery Manager is empowered to:   
 Allocate Workday delivery resources across approved priorities and commitments.   
 Manage Workday delivery sequencing within established business priorities, and recommend sequencing changes when demand exceeds capacity.   
 Determine whether sufficient capacity and capability exist before accepting delivery commitments.   
 Hold AMS and delivery partners accountable for performance and resource quality, and require replacement or remediation plans for vendor resources that consistently do not meet expectations.   
 Make routine operational and delivery decisions without VP-level intervention.   
 Escalate cross-platform technical risks to the Technical Delivery Lead and architecture decisions to the HCM Architect.   
 Escalate material priority, funding, or business trade-offs with clear options and recommendations.   
 Basic Requirements   
 8+ years of progressive experience delivering Workday or comparable enterprise HCM solutions.   
 Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Human Resources, Business, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.   
 Demonstrated experience with Workday application delivery, enhancement management, AMS, and production support.   
 Proven experience managing resource capacity, allocation, and competing priorities across mixed internal and vendor delivery teams without direct reporting authority.   
 Experience leading PI Planning and managing multiple concurrent PI commitments, enhancements, production demands, and projects.   
 Strong working knowledge of Workday configuration, security, integrations, testing, and release management.   
 Strong understanding of incident, problem, change, release, and service-management disciplines.   
 Demonstrated ability to translate business demand into realistic resource and delivery plans.   
 Preferred Skills/Experience   
 Workday certifications and/or deep hands-on experience in the relevant Workday functional or technical domain (strongly preferred).   
 Experience managing global onshore/offshore delivery models and managed-service providers.   
 Experience with Agile delivery practices and ServiceNow-based service management.   
 Familiarity with SOX/ITGC, privacy, and audit requirements affecting HR technologies.   
 Strong vendor, stakeholder, and executive communication skills.   
 Ability to make decisions, manage trade-offs, and hold delivery teams and partners accountable for outcomes through influence.   
 Measures of Success   
 PI commitments delivered predictably with appropriate quality.   
 Resource capacity aligned to the highest-priority business outcomes.   
 Improved accuracy of resource forecasts and delivery commitments.   
 Capacity constraints and skill gaps identified before they affect delivery.   
 Reduced resource bottlenecks and dependence on individual SMEs.   
 Improved Workday platform stability, with fewer recurring incidents and a reduced AMS backlog.   
 Improved AMS resource capability, continuity, and accountability.   
 Small-to-medium initiatives delivered without unnecessary executive intervention.   
 Increased use of standard Workday capabilities and reduced avoidable technical debt.

Fidus is a global high-tech design firm headquartered in Ottawa, with additional design centres in Kitchener-Waterloo and San Jose. We specialize in leading-edge electronic product development, with hardware, embedded software, FPGA/ASIC, and signal integrity teams working together to design and deliver next-generation products for clients in emerging technology markets.
 Position Overview/Mandate: 
 The FPGA Designer plays a key role in designing and delivering complex FPGA-based systems for Fidus clients. You will work directly with customers and internal Fidus teams to define architectures, implement RTL, integrate IP, run simulations, close timing, and support lab bring-up and debug.
 This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working with new FPGA families and tools, is comfortable moving between different application domains (video, communications, storage, signal processing), and takes pride in producing high-quality, well-documented designs.
 Make an Impact with US: 
 At Fidus, you'll work on high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems, often using emerging technologies before they reach the broader market. You'll collaborate across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design as part of cross-functional teams delivering real products for our clients.
 In practice, that means contributing to projects across Communications, Aerospace & Defence, Life Sciences & Medical Devices, Space & Satellite, Industrial Automation, Automotive, and Semiconductor engagements. You won't be limited to a single product or industry—your work will follow the technology, not just one roadmap.
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Work with our clients and other Fidus Employees to develop complex FPGA and/or CPLD based systems, including architecture, custom development, integrated IP, simulations, and timing analysis and closure.
 Design FPGA based systems using Xilinx and Intel based devices and tools
 Participate in design reviews (hardware-software interface, input-outputs etc.) to ensure Fidus quality standards and customer requirements are being adhered to
 Perform lab testing, debug of prototypes and supporting hardware/software engineer, as needed
 Perform customer prototype demonstrations and author test plans, design description and user documentation
 Provide technical insight to customers during the pre-sales and implementation phase of projects
 Provide technical support to the Business Manager and Sales team by providing detailed estimates on project scope, schedule, and deliverables and to present the technical aspects of Fidus proposals to the client
 Who You are: 
 Minimum 5 years of experience designing using RTL/Verilog/VHDL on FPGAs.
 Experience with video systems and specification standards, video algorithms, and high-speed memory and bus interfaces, communications protocols, and DSP or processor instantiations.
 Created designs using Xilinx or Altera FPGA families and have a solid understanding of tool flow
 Experience with Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL, Xilinx Vivado, Altera Quartus, and/or ModelSim
 RTL design and verification including test benches, functional simulations, and timing closure
 Exhibit strong communication skills, are fluent in English, have great customer interaction presence, and quickly learn new technologies and processes
 Proven techniques and habits that lead to high quality design
 Embraces AI as part of a modern engineering toolkit
 Degree as a B.A.Sc., B.Eng. or equivalent

Executive Operations (Exec Ops) Chief of Staff Track, 12–18 Months) 
 If you’re a highly organized, extremely self-accountable, love project management (think Trello/Asana), and desire to grow into the 2nd in command of a fast growing startup… then this might just be your dream job. 
 My name is Richard Yu, I’m the founder/CEO of a fast-growing education + software business. 
 Across all social, my media team and I have built a 1.5M+ follower platform (@richardyuzee on IG, as an example).
 My #1 responsibility is to spend 40 hours/week being the talent (face of our content), and visionary (having long blocks of 4 hrs/day) where I can think about vision and growth strategies.
 That means I need to spend all my time creating content, driving strategy, and making high-leverage decisions… and this is where you come in.
 Your job is to protect my time, eliminate operational drag, and make sure the company actually executes.
 This role is Exec Ops / Office of the CEO — think of it as a supercharged Executive Assistant with a real path to Chief of Staff, based on performance. You will be my execution arm and second brain, with high trust, high access, and high expectations.
 This is not a “cute admin” job. It’s also not a glamorous strategy-only job. It’s the real work: calendar, follow-ups, accountability, systems, project management, hiring ops, and getting things done
 What you’ll own (your responsibilities)
 1) CEO Time + Calendar (your #1 responsibility)
 Own my calendar ruthlessly: protect deep work blocks, batch meetings, enforce priorities
 Gate time, not people (you’re not allowed to be a “gatekeeper” personality)
 Turn chaos into an intentional weekly schedule that matches company goals
 2) Internal Communication + Follow-Up
 Run the follow-up engine: action items, owners, due dates, reminders, escalation
 Ensure nothing dies in Slack/WhatsApp/email because people “got busy”
 Draft messages/emails and internal updates so I can approve quickly
 3) Project Management + Accountability (across the whole org)
 Build/quarterback the company operating system (Trello/Asana/Notion—whatever we standardize)
 Every project has: owner, deadline, next action, definition of done
 Hold leaders accountable (ex: Moe accountable to deliverables, Bashar accountable to reporting cadence, content team accountable to output)
 4) Hiring Operations (big focus right now)
 Run end-to-end hiring ops for key roles: Organic Content Director, Senior DR Copywriter/Head of Marketing, IG Copywriter, etc.
 Manage pipeline, scheduling, scorecards, assignments, Loom reviews, references
 Keep the process moving fast without me getting dragged into logistics
 5) Content Operations Oversight (not creating content)
 Ensure content machines ship on time: YouTube, IG, email—whatever is on the calendar gets done on time. 
 Track weekly output + deadlines + approvals so I’m not chasing people 
 You must be insanely detail oriented and VERY good at calling people out and holding them accountable. 
 6) Metrics + Reporting
 Monthly P&L request/collection, KPI dashboards, and weekly reporting rhythm
 You will analyze the Profit & Loss statement every month, analyze the payroll (yes you will know how much everyone gets paid), and provide extremely detailed recommendations on who should get raises, comp structure adjustments, who is being inefficient, who needs to get cut, etc. 
 7) Personal + Local Projects (as needed)
 Help execute real-life projects that support business performance (ex: managing the build-out of a home studio in Puerto Rico)
 Spanish is preferred because it helps with local execution, but it’s not required. If you’re insanely quick with a translator / ChatGPT for messages, works as well. 
 8) AI Emphasis 
 You should come with batteries included with understanding how to use AI in your workflow. The most BASIC version of this is ChatGPT instead of using Google, that’s the bare bare minimum. 
 You should be so good with AI that you are now giving feedback and suggestions to OTHER department leaders on how they should be using AI in their day to day responsiblities. 
 What success looks like (KPIs)
 20+ hours/week of my time returned within 60–90 days
 I stop doing: project management, follow-ups, DM appointment setting, internal chasing, hiring logistics
 Weekly operating rhythm runs without me pushing it
 Projects move faster, less stress, fewer dropped balls
 The company becomes calmer and more accountable — not more chaotic
 Who this is for
 This is for you if:
 You’re an operator: you love execution, structure, and turning chaos into order
 You have extreme ownership: you don’t wait to be told, you anticipate
 You can make good decisions without asking me every day for permission.
 You’re comfortable being in the background while I’m front-facing in the content
 You’re discreet and trustworthy (you will see everything)
 You’re strong at writing and communication (VERY detailed reports, clear, direct)
 You enjoy running a tight system and holding people accountable
 Who this is NOT for
 This is not for you if:
 You want a “strategy-only” role where you get to “bounce ideas” with Richard without doing admin, follow-ups, or nitty-gritty execution
 You need constant direction, reassurance, or step-by-step instructions where you get “coaching” from Richard (FYI - you’re here to protect my time, not get “free mentorship” from Richard).
 You avoid conflict and can’t hold people accountable in tough conversations when they’re late or underperforming 
 You’re not comfortable with high access + high confidentiality
 You get offended by doing “unsexy” tasks — this role includes them. 
 Example: 3-4 hour project of looking at every single expense item on Richard’s AMEX credit card statement to identify for software and expenses that we are overpaying on, and then reaching out to each software company to cancel them. 
 You should be smart to DO IT ONCE, and either build a system to automate this, delegate to someone else, or you just own this ongoing monthly moving forward. 
 The truth: the trade-off (good, bad, and ugly)
 You will get full context: you’ll see my schedule, meetings, priorities, and how decisions get made in real time. This is high-speed CEO training.
 In exchange, you will also do the work I genuinely don’t want to do:
 Following up, reminding, pushing projects forward
 coordinating hiring logistics and keeping candidates moving along by messaging them on iMessage and Whatsapp on my behalf
 Collecting metrics, reports, and making sure people deliver
 Dealing with repetitive tasks that protect my creative bandwidth
 If that trade-off excites you, you’ll love this role.
 Ramp / onboarding plan (how you’ll get trained)
 Phase 1 — Shadowing + Context (Weeks 1–4)
 You shadow everything: calendar, meetings, comms, priorities
 You build the “Richard OS”: how I think, what matters, how I decide
 You start taking small tasks immediately (scheduling, notes, action items)
 Phase 2 — Execution + Systems (Days 30–60)
 You take ownership of the follow-up engine + task system
 You run weekly planning with me (short, structured)
 You begin managing hiring ops and key cross-functional projects
 You enforce owners/due dates and begin reducing my stress load
 Phase 3 — Office of the CEO Operator (Days 60–90)
 You run the operating cadence: reporting, follow-ups, meeting prep

 At the heart of great partnerships we’ll always find EMPATHY
 WHAT IS YOUR ROLE
 As a Senior Accounts Receivable Associate, you will support the Invoice to Cash (I2C) team by serving as the research and resolution engine behind the Collections and Cash Application teams. You will own the JIRA queue end to end, conduct account reconciliations, coordinate with internal teams to investigate and resolve inquiries, and provide findings that are either fully resolved or ready for the collector to communicate to the customer.
 You will work in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift daily and ticket volumes are high. Your work will range from quick account lookups to complex, multi-system reconciliations involving Stripe, NetSuite, Tesorio, and multiple internal stakeholders. You will play an important role in protecting front-line capacity and ensuring that issues are thoroughly investigated and brought to resolution.
 WHY DO WE WANT YOU
 We are currently looking for impact-driven individuals who are passionate about helping Boldr grow and achieve our Purpose. We expect our Team to become our ultimate partners to success by always giving their 110% in everything, sharing their talents and quirks, and championing our core values: Curious, Dynamic, and Authentic.

 Own the AR JIRA queue. Triage, investigate, and resolve internal tickets within team SLAs. You are the named owner from open to close, including chasing down whoever you need across Billing, Sales Ops, RevOps, Tax, or Support to get an answer.
 Absorb research and reconciliation work from the front line. Any investigation that would pull a collector or CashApp analyst off their book gets routed to you. You dig in, document what you find, and return it in one of two states: fully resolved with the internal stakeholder, or written up as a customer-ready response the front-line agent can send without rework.
 Run account reconciliations. Tie out customer ledgers across Stripe, our billing systems, and the GL when payments, credits, or balances do not match what the customer expects.
 Support Cash Application. Take on payment research, unapplied cash investigation, and ad hoc recon work for the CashApp team under the same handoff model.
 Handle limited direct customer contact.  Spot the patterns. When the same issue keeps showing up in the queue, flag it. Part of the value of this seat is seeing the recurring breaks before anyone else does.

 Able to handle and prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
 Highly self-motivated 
 Able to maintain confidentiality and exercise extreme discretion.
 Honest and Trustworthy.
 Able to adapt to change and learn quickly
 Detail-oriented
 You are able to work onsite full time
 You are able to adapt to schedule changes (Primary schedule follows US business hour, but schedule may change depending on operational needs)
 YOU HAVE…
 At a minimum, an associate's degree in Accounting or a related field

About Clutch: 
 We’re on a mission to reinvent the way people buy, sell, and own cars. Are you game?
 Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car buying and selling experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee… and that’s just the beginning.
 Named six years in a row to the Globe & Mail’s Top Growing Companies in Canada and Deloitte Technology Fast 50/Fast 500 lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team.
 Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including D1 Capital, Canaan, Real Ventures, BrandProject, and Upper90. To learn more, visit clutch.ca.
 About the role: 
 Clutch is looking for an experienced Paintless Dent Repair (PDR) Technician to join our growing Vehicle Reconditioning team!
 As a PDR Technician, you’ll be responsible for repairing dents and cosmetic damage to a high retail standard while preserving the vehicle’s original factory finish. You’ll work at one indoor location with a steady, scheduled flow of vehicles, allowing you to focus on the work without the need for estimating, customer communication, invoicing, or collections.
 Every vehicle you work on will ultimately be delivered to a Clutch customer, making quality and attention to detail an important part of the role.
 What you’ll do: 
 Repair dents to a high retail cosmetic standard using traditional rod work, glue pulling, and knockdowns
 Repair a variety of damage including door dings, body lines, sharp dents, and hail damage
 Assess incoming damage and determine whether it is suitable for PDR or should be referred to body and refinish
 Remove and reinstall trim, liners, and hardware to access factory openings
 Perform repairs through existing factory access points such as window apertures, plug holes, and grommets
 Use glue pulling techniques where traditional tool access is limited
 Do not drill access holes or modify vehicles without written pre-approval
 Document repairs with before-and-after photos
 Inspect completed repairs under proper lighting to ensure they meet Clutch’s quality standards
 Identify and flag damage that falls outside of PDR scope before the vehicle moves through the reconditioning process
 Work closely with detailers, body technicians, estimators, and other members of the reconditioning team
 Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area
 Consistently deliver high-quality repairs while maintaining efficient production
 What we’re looking for: 
 2+ years of professional Paintless Dent Repair experience
 Demonstrated experience repairing door dings, body lines, and sharp dents
 Strong traditional rod work and glue pulling skills
 Strong understanding of PDR repairability and the ability to accurately assess a panel before beginning work
 Ability to work efficiently while maintaining a high standard of quality
 Strong attention to detail and pride in your workmanship
 Ability to consistently meet quality and production expectations
 Strong communication and teamwork skills
 Ability to work independently and take ownership of your work
 Valid driver’s license, as you may be required to move vehicles around the site
 Other items to note: 
 This is an indoor, single-site position
 You’ll work with a consistent, scheduled flow of vehicles
 Vehicles arrive with damage already identified and photographed
 Repairs must preserve the vehicle’s original factory finish
 Access holes must not be drilled into vehicles
 Any damage outside of PDR scope should be identified and escalated early
 A practical assessment on real vehicles will be part of the hiring process
 It’d be great if you have: 
 Experience repairing aluminum panels
 Experience with hail damage
 Previous dealership, collision repair, or vehicle reconditioning experience
 Experience working within documented repair standards or tiered rate structures
 Why you’ll love it at Clutch: 
 Consistent work: Enjoy a steady, scheduled flow of vehicles without needing to find your own work
 Focus on your craft: Spend your time repairing vehicles instead of handling sales, estimating, invoicing, collections, or customer communication
 Indoor work: Work at one location without seasonal travel or chasing hail work
 Quality-focused environment: Take pride in delivering high-quality repairs that are virtually invisible to the customer
 Great team: Work alongside experienced technicians, detailers, estimators, and other reconditioning professionals
 Competitive compensation: Earn $30.00–$40.00 per hour , based on experience and qualifications
 Benefits: Access comprehensive health and dental benefits
 Growth opportunities: Join a growing reconditioning operation with opportunities to develop your skills and take on additional responsibility
 Specialized trade: Build your career in a specialized PDR role within a growing automotive company
 Employment Type: 
 New, Permanent Full-Time
 Compensation & Benefits: 
 Wage: $30.00 - $40.00 per hour 
 Comprehensive benefits plans include healthcare, dental care, vision care, prescriptions, life insurance, and dependent coverage; start from day 1. (Applicable for Permanent Full-Time)
 Pay decisions reflect objective criteria: skills, performance, market benchmarking, responsibilities, and working conditions
 Clutch is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where all individuals have an opportunity to succeed. If you require accommodation at any stage of the interview process, please email talent@clutch.ca .

À propos de Futurpreneur      
 Futurpreneur est un organisme national à but non lucratif qui habilite les jeunes entrepreneur.e.s de divers horizons, âgé.e.s de 18 à 39 ans, à démarrer, acheter et développer leurs entreprises au Canada, en leur offrant des prêts avec du mentorat et des ressources.
 Fondé en 1996, nous avons aidé plus de 20 000 jeunes entrepreneur.e.s à lancer plus de 15 600 entreprises, en faisant de l'entrepreneuriat chez les jeunes Canadien.ne.s, un pilier essentiel pour renforcer l'économie tout en générant des opportunités d'emploi et favoriser un avenir durable.
 Futurpreneur est un membre fondateur de l’ Alliance des jeunes entrepreneur.e.s du G20 , le représentant canadien du réseau Youth Business International et l’hôte canadien de la Semaine mondiale de l’entrepreneuriat .
 Notre but (notre raison d’être) : favoriser la prospérité inclusive au Canada en soutenant le succès des jeunes entrepreneur.e.s.     
 Notre mission (ce que nous faisons chaque jour pour atteindre notre objectif) : Autonomiser les entrepreneur.e.s issus de divers horizons âgé.e.s de 18 à 39 ans en leur fournissant des prêts assortis de mentorat et de ressources pour les aider à démarrer ou à acheter des entreprises à succès qui contribuent à la prospérité économique durable et inclusive, dans leurs communautés et à travers le Canada.
 Nos valeurs (notre manière de travailler, nos principes fondamentaux et nos engagements) : nous sommes motivés par notre mission et travaillons dans un esprit de collégialité et de collaboration, de diversité et d’inclusion, de responsabilité et de transparence.     
 L’opportunité : 
 En tant qu’ analyste-conseil en entrepreneuriat bilingue, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel dans la croissance continue du succès de l'organisation. Vous aurez la responsabilité d'aider les entrepreneurs à créer et à développer des demandes de financement réussies pour les programmes et services de Futurpreneur, tout en maintenant un niveau exceptionnel de satisfaction de la clientèle et en vous assurant que les objectifs régionaux sont atteints et/ou dépassés.  
 Ce poste existant est un poste à temps plein, permanent, basé à Montreal, QC, ou Toronto, ON ou Vancouver, BC. Le titulaire travaillera selon un modèle hybride, nécessitant un minimum de 2 jours par semaine au bureau.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Présélection des entrepreneurs  
 ·       Passer en revue les demandes, notamment le plan d'affaires et les flux de trésorerie, afin de déterminer l'admissibilité aux programmes et au financement 
 ·       Communiquer les inadéquations potentielles en regard de l'admissibilité (dont le plan d'affaires, l'industrie, les budgets de caisse, etc.) 
 ·       Effectuer des analyses de rapport de solvabilité afin de déterminer si les entrepreneurs sont admissibles aux financements de Futurpreneur Canada ou d'un partenaire de cofinancement 
 ·       Déterminer les limites de financement et communiquer les problèmes de crédit aux entrepreneurs afin d'améliorer leurs connaissances financières
 Demandes d’inscription au programme, consultation avec les entrepreneurs  
 ·       Examiner les demandes, y compris les plans d'affaires et les flux de trésorerie, pour déterminer la viabilité des entreprises et aider les entrepreneurs à mettre à jour leur demande afin qu'elles répondent aux normes de Futurpreneur Canada 
 ·       Évaluer les demandes d’inscription et fournir des rétroactions nécessaires afin d’élaborer des plans d'affaires et des flux de trésorerie viables qui répondent aux exigences de Futurpreneur 
 ·       Compiler et évaluer toute la documentation additionnelle requise pour déposer des demandes de financement complètes au département d'évaluation du crédit national 
 ·       Évaluer les forces et les capacités des postulant(e)s et les aiguiller vers des ressources précises
 ·       Résumer les renseignements pertinents qui ne se trouvent pas dans la demande et qui auront une incidence sur les évaluations effectuées par le département d'évaluation du crédit 
 ·       Évaluer le déroulement du travail en fonction de la qualité (du travail et des demandeurs) et prévoir les mois ou les dates potentielles de décaissement
 Demandes d’inscription au programme, consultation avec les partenaires locaux

 ·       Répondre aux questions des partenaires, relatives aux demandes 
 ·       Examiner les demandes déposées par les partenaires locaux afin de déterminer la viabilité à l'aide du Prédicteur de risque de l’entreprise (PRE) et des exigences de Futurpreneur 
 ·       Passer en revue les demandes pour déterminer s'il manque des documents requis habituellement collectés par le partenaire local 
 ·       Aider les partenaires locaux à accompagner les entrepreneurs dans la compréhension des prérequis tels que les documents nécessaires et les délais habituels 
 ·       Apporter un soutien aux gestionnaires des communauté entrepreneuriales dans la formation des partenaires locaux sur les détails des différents programmes et les aiguiller afin de soumettre des demandes d’inscription de qualité 
 ·       Résumer les renseignements pertinents qui ne se trouvent pas dans la demande et qui auront une incidence sur les évaluations effectuées par l'équipe d’évaluation du crédit 
 ·       Déposer la demande dûment remplie à l'équipe d’évaluation du crédit 
 Demande d’inscription – Conditions  
 ·       Préparer et communiquer l'acceptation au programme et les conditions en suspens nécessaires au décaissement 
 ·       Recueillir et évaluer les documents conditionnels requis 
 ·       S’assurer que les demandes de mentorat soient acheminées à l’équipe des associés en mentorat 
 ·       Accompagner l’entrepreneur à compléter une séance d'orientation en ligne sur le mentorat 
 ·       Préparer, signer et soumettre les accords de prêt, les billets à ordre et autres documents juridiques requis

 ·       Travailler directement avec les équipes d’évaluation du crédit ; d’entrepreneur-en-résidence et de conformité pour s'assurer que les demandes des entrepreneurs respectent les critères d'admissibilité 
 ·       Consulter l'équipe des gestionnaires des communautés entrepreneuriales sur les stratégies visant à accroître l'intérêt des mentors et des entrepreneurs 
 ·       Autres tâches telles qu'assignées

 ·       Expertise en analyse financière
 ·       Expertise dans le service à la clientèle et désir d’assister la clientèle 
 ·       Compétences exemplaires dans l’atteinte des objectifs organisationnels 
 ·       Approche proactive dans la résolution des conflits 
 ·       Excellente attention aux détails

 ·       Confiance et grande motivation personnelle 
 ·       Capacité démontrée à travailler efficacement sous pression dans un environnement dynamique
 ·       S’aligner avec les valeurs de Futurpreneur et dévoué à la mission/objectif de l'organisation

 Chez Futurpreneur, nous offrons un ensemble complet d’avantages sociaux conçu pour soutenir votre bien-être, votre croissance professionnelle et votre équilibre travail-vie personnelle.

Nous investissons également dans l’apprentissage et le développement grâce à une allocation d’apprentissage, un programme de coaching et un accès à une plateforme d’apprentissage en ligne.

veritree and Job Overview
 veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.
 veritree is seeking a Project Manager, Terrestrial, to own our North American terrestrial reforestation portfolio end-to-end, along with a small number of global terrestrial accounts. This is a hands-on relationship and process role: you will run the day-to-day relationships with multiple planting partners across Canada and the United States, keeping monitoring on track, ensuring partners follow our processes, and building and refining the standard operating procedures (SOPs) that govern how terrestrial projects run. 
 This role suits a Registered Professional Forester who is organized, comfortable running multiple partner relationships at once, keeping monitoring programs on schedule, and developing the processes that make results repeatable. We value candidates who are direct, transparent, and accountable.
 Given this is a hybrid role based in Vancouver, BC, priority will be given to local candidates who are able to work from our office on a hybrid basis.
 6 Month Key Outcomes (6m KOs)
 Own the end-to-end relationships with all of our terrestrial planting partners, running recurring business reviews, triaging field issues, and following through consistently so partners experience veritree as organized, transparent, and dependable.
 Ensure data collection and monitoring is on track across every account: high-integrity planting data, survival checks scheduled and completed on an annual cadence, and partners following our processes consistently.
 Finish, document, and stabilize the core terrestrial SOP set (planting session, evidence requirements, survival monitoring) and make it repeatable across partners and regions.
 What You'll Do
 Account & Relationship Management
 Manage multiple terrestrial planting partner relationships in parallel and serve as the primary point of contact.
 Manage a small number of global terrestrial accounts (for example, in the Philippines and Australia), applying the same standards and processes, and supporting the corporate partners who fund them.
 Own and run all recurring partner meetings and business reviews: setting agendas, driving decisions, and owning follow-through.
 Communicate clearly, concisely, and transparently with partners operating across different contexts, and be accountable for every commitment made internally or externally.
 Triage issues that arise in the field and coordinate the right internal teams to resolve them.
 Travel to planting sites for audits and partner visits as needed.
 Experience flying drones and processing data is an asset. 
 Data, Monitoring & Tree Tracking
 Keep each partner's planting, monitoring, and survival data accurate and current: owning data hygiene and quality checks on data flowing into our system.
 Make sure monitoring tasks (survival checks at defined intervals, with first survival reports one year after planting) are created, scheduled, and completed across all accounts.
 Manage outstanding monitoring backlogs with a prioritized, batched plan, and provide regular status updates on progress against targets.
 SOPs & Process
 Create, refine, and audit the SOPs that define what we expect of terrestrial projects: from planting sessions and evidence requirements to survival monitoring.
 Hold partners to the process: make sure each account follows our SOPs consistently, and work with partners to close gaps where they aren't.
 Write SOPs at a level general enough to adapt across regions, species, and partner capacity, so they can be standardized across all terrestrial projects.
 Requirements 
 Qualifications
 Professional Requirements or Qualifications 
 Registered Professional Forester (RPF) or Registered Forest Technologist designation, or eligibility for registration.
 Bachelor's degree or technical diploma in forestry, silviculture, environmental science, or a related discipline.
 Hands-on North American reforestation experience: planting operations, silviculture, or forest monitoring.
 Strong knowledge of North American tree species and reforestation practices.
 Demonstrated project or account management experience, including managing multiple external partners in parallel and delivering on timelines.
 Highly organized: able to keep monitoring schedules, follow-ups, and processes on track across multiple accounts at once.
 Ability to travel within North America, with occasional international travel (10-15% of time).
 Personal Strengths 
 Strong people skills: builds trust quickly and maintains healthy long-term partner relationships.
 Highly accountable and consistent: you do what you say you will do.
 Clear and concise communicator, especially in cross-cultural partner relationships.
 Comfortable building structure and process in a fast-moving startup environment.
 Nice to Haves (not mandatory) 
 Hands-on experience with UAV (drone) operations, including flight planning, image processing, and imagery analysis, is an asset.
 Experience working with Indigenous partnerships and community-led restoration.
 Familiarity with carbon or MRV/MMRV monitoring workflows.
 People management or mentoring experience.
 Benefits 
 Benefits & Compensation Overview
 At veritree, we recognize that compensation and performance development are key to attracting and retaining top talent. Our approach is grounded in fairness, transparency, and creating opportunities for growth as both our people and business scale.
 Some highlights you can expect include:
 Competitive salary with a performance-driven framework that ensures fair and consistent compensation reviews, tied to individual impact and business growth
 Extended health, dental, and vision benefits
 Additional Health Spending Account (HSA) / Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) to support your well-being and lifestyle interests
 A variety of time-off programs, including vacation, personal days, and a 4-week remote work program each year
 Employee discount with tentree, our sister company
 A flexible, hybrid work environment designed for collaboration and focus-driven impact
 veritree ensures that compensation is reviewed fairly and consistently, with opportunities for salary progression tied to sustained performance. As such, the salary range for this role is $90,000 to $120,000 CAD. 
 This range is positioned around the 50th–75th percentile of market data we've collected, reflecting our commitment to competitive pay. Final offer amounts are based on individual experience and skillset of the candidate demonstrated during the recruitment process.
 We reserve the >75th percentile of our salary ranges for internal employees who demonstrate sustained high performance and impact at veritree.
 veritree is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business needs.

 Talent Pipeline Posting Notice

 We are seeking a Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help support the execution of lighting work across GameSim projects.

In addition to completing assigned lighting work, you may help coordinate tasks, review the work of other artists, provide constructive feedback, and ensure scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.

 What Success Looks Like

 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, lighting pipeline, gameplay requirements, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, and other project disciplines.
 Create polished lighting work that meets the project’s established visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for assigned scenes, environments, sequences, or gameplay areas.
 Provide useful feedback and support to other artists when asked to review or coordinate lighting work.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and communicate them to the appropriate project leads.
 Deliver assigned work on schedule and respond effectively to internal and client feedback.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.

 Respond to feedback from Art Direction, project leadership, and clients in a timely and professional manner.
 Ensure completed work meets project requirements for quality, performance, organization, and delivery.

ABOUT VALSOFT VENTURES 
 Valsoft is a Montreal-based company that acquires and grows vertical market software businesses, with a portfolio of 140+ companies that spans dozens of industries and countries. Valsoft Ventures is where we build new companies from scratch. Each venture starts with a founder in residence and runs on Valsoft’s capital, infrastructure, and support, and its first customers often come from inside Valsoft’s own portfolio.
 THE OPPORTUNITY 
 We’re looking for a Tax Manager to own tax for the companies Ventures builds (currently 4). You’ll set each new company up correctly from the start, keep it compliant as it grows, and build the process every future venture follows. The work centres on Canada and the U.S., with filings elsewhere coordinated through local advisors as ventures enter new markets.
 In one week you might register a new entity, review a U.S. state return for an older venture, and walk a founder in residence through what QST means for their first Quebec customer. The hard part is that every venture is different and none of them waits for tax. Founders move fast, priorities shift when a venture changes direction, and you’ll often set up a company whose product isn’t finished yet.
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You’re responsible for the quality of the result.
 WHAT YOU’LL DO 
 Set up each new venture correctly. When Ventures decides to build a company, you’ll work out what tax needs to be in place before it takes its first customer: structuring input, registrations, elections, and how its products and pricing are taxed. You’ll work with the founder in residence, Valsoft’s finance and legal teams, and the VP, Tax on structuring decisions.
 Run compliance across the ventures. Manage Canadian federal and provincial corporate income tax returns and U.S. federal and state income and franchise tax returns for each venture, reviewing what external providers prepare. Keep a tax calendar, records, and audit files for every company, and resolve notices and correspondence from the CRA, Revenu Québec, the IRS, and state authorities.
 Own sales and indirect tax. Own U.S. sales and use tax for the ventures: nexus monitoring, registrations, taxability analysis, filing, and remittance. In Canada, manage GST/HST and QST, including registrations, returns, and input tax credit and input tax refund recovery.
 Handle intercompany and group reporting. Ventures run on Valsoft’s capital, infrastructure, and support, which means intercompany arrangements from the first day. Set up and document those arrangements, coordinate transfer pricing documentation with external advisors in line with CRA, IRS, and OECD guidelines, and support any inquiries.
 Build the tax process Ventures runs on. Design the processes, controls, and tools that let tax keep up as the number of ventures grows, and decide where a tax engine or automation is worth adding. Founders, finance, and legal will treat you as their main contact on tax, and you’ll explain requirements in plain terms.
 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR 
 A CPA designation (Canada or U.S.) and at least 4 years of post-designation tax experience in public accounting or a corporate tax environment, with exposure to both Canadian and U.S. tax.
 Working knowledge of transfer pricing, international tax, and tax accounting under IFRS.
 You can look at a new business model and work out what tax it triggers before it launches, and give a founder a clear answer they can act on the same day.
 You prepare, review, and file returns yourself, and you manage external advisors and hold them to deadlines and quality.
 You use AI to research, draft, and analyze, and you check the output before it goes anywhere.
 You work independently, keep several companies’ calendars moving at once, finish what you start, and keep records an auditor can follow.
 USEFUL EXPERIENCE 
 Hands-on U.S. sales and use tax compliance, and Canadian GST/HST and QST compliance
 Tax for startups or newly formed entities, including the sales tax treatment of software and SaaS
 Voluntary disclosures
 Working in a group with many subsidiaries
 WHAT WE VALUE 
 Sound judgment and attention to detail.
 Taking responsibility and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how a young company makes money and how tax follows it.
 Curiosity and a willingness to change an approach that isn’t working.
 The honesty to say when a position isn’t defensible, including your own.
 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE 
 Within your first six months, every existing venture has a current tax calendar, the registrations it needs, a sales tax nexus review, and an audit file someone else could pick up.
 The next company Ventures launches goes through your setup checklist and charges the right tax on its first invoice.
 Intercompany arrangements are documented, and Valsoft’s corporate tax team gets provision and group reporting inputs from you on time.
 By the end of your first year, founders bring you in before they change pricing or enter a new market, not after. A founder mentions a new pricing model on Monday, and by Wednesday you’ve worked out where it creates nexus and what the invoice needs to say.

 À PROPOS DE VALSOFT VENTURES 
 Valsoft est une entreprise montréalaise qui acquiert et fait croître des entreprises de logiciels de marchés verticaux, avec un portefeuille de plus de 140 entreprises couvrant des dizaines de secteurs d’activité et de pays..  About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 
 About the team 
 The Link Partnerships team sources, develops, and manages relationships with the payments ecosystem partners that power Link, Stripe's consumer wallet. Our team drives the growth and utility of Link by building partnerships with card networks, card issuers, local payment methods, crypto providers, and emerging commerce platforms. We execute on high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that expand Link's acceptance, improve performance, and enable new payment experiences—including agentic commerce. These partnerships have a significant impact on Stripe and the products used by millions of our users.
 What you’ll do 
 We're looking for a Partner Development Manager who builds and manages Link's payments partnerships with card networks, card issuers, local payment method providers, and crypto and stablecoin providers. You'll own the strategy and execution of partnerships that expand Link's payment capabilities, improve transaction performance, and position Link as the default payments layer for agentic commerce. You'll negotiate commercial agreements, drive technical integrations, and shape Link's payments roadmap in collaboration with these partners. As part of these efforts, you'll collaborate closely with cross-functional stakeholders, including Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Risk, and others. You'll also lead relationship management and partner closely with external partners' executive leadership.
 Responsibilities 
 Define and execute Link's payments partnership strategy across card networks, card issuers, local payment methods, and crypto and stablecoins
 Negotiate and manage commercial agreements with payment partners that expand Link's acceptance footprint, improve authorization rates, and unlock new payment capabilities
 Develop a deep understanding of the card network and issuer landscape—including scheme rules, tokenization frameworks, authentication protocols, and competitive dynamics—to inform partnership strategy

Rockstar is recruiting for a leading organization dedicated to advancing decentralized finance (DeFi) through innovative protocol engineering and product design. The client is a mission-driven foundation supporting the growth, decentralization, and sustainability of the Uniswap ecosystem, with a focus on driving value across protocol innovation, developer support, governance, research, and security. This role offers the opportunity to work at the forefront of DeFi, collaborating with a team committed to building impactful, open financial infrastructure.
 v4 Hooks Architect 
 A senior builder is sought who operates at the intersection of protocol engineering and DeFi product design. This individual will design, prototype, and productionize Uniswap v4 hooks that unlock new markets. Areas of focus include dynamic fee markets, JIT‑aware liquidity protections, programmable compliance for RWAs, solver/intents integrations, perps/credit primitives, and beyond.
 Why this role exists 
 - Hooks are the frontier. Uniswap v4 turns AMM behavior into a programmable surface. The ecosystem needs more production-ready hooks to go from tinkering to real usage.
 - Builders need partners. High‑quality hooks require deep protocol knowledge and product instincts designing the onchain mechanics, the incentives, and a path to distribution.
 - The mandate: accelerate onchain trading activity and protocol support across Uniswap deployments. This role is central to that impact.
 The work 
 - Bring product thinking for market‑tailored hooks: Ideate/incubate high‑leverage ideas across market segments: volatile pairs (ETH/USDx, xBTC/USDx), correlated/stable pairs (USDx–USDx), and order sizes from small retail to whales. Translate these insights into concrete hook specs with clear adoption and measurement plans.
 - Architect & ship hooks: Own the full lifecycle from whiteboard to an audited mainnet deployment that advances the roadmap (fee dynamics, liquidity management, MEV/LVR capture, KYC/attestations, JIT, etc.).
 - Author canonical patterns: Publish reference implementations, hook templates, and “living specs” that other teams can safely extend.
 - Design with distribution in mind: Co‑create adoption plans with other DeFi protocols (lending/ALMs/vaults), aggregators/routers, intent layers, asset issuers. Ship the adapters, simulators, and SDK glue to make integration easy.
 - Own security & correctness: Threat model hooks, define invariants, fuzz and formally verify critical paths, and partner with external auditors.
 - Data & feedback loops: Work with the data team to instrument events/metrics, write Dune/Flipside dashboards, and run controlled experiments to tune parameters (fees, tick ranges, JIT thresholds) based on observed flow, MEV, and LP PnL.
 A week in this role might look like 
 - Ideate, architect, and implement a new stable‑stable hook designed to win $100k+ trades (market‑share target, slippage/fee behavior, routing incentives, aggregator integration plan).
 - Design abstractions for reusability and code hygiene. Upstream libraries into a canonical toolkit.
 - Pair programming and code reviews with an external team on a lending rehypothecation hook design and implementation.
 - Write Foundry tests and fuzzers for beforeSwap/afterSwap invariants; benchmark gas and optimize with Yul where it pays.
 - Coordinate with an aggregator on simulation support and revert reasons; land a PR to their router.
 What success looks like 
 3 months
 - Land one high‑leverage hook in audit or on testnet with credible distribution partners.
 - Establish a metrics schema and dashboard framework for hook evaluation (LP PnL, orderflow capture, effective liquidity).
 6 months
 - Two production hooks with measurable flow/TVL and zero critical incidents.
 - Clear adoption playbooks for routers, wallets, and solver layers; at least three third‑party teams shipping on these patterns.
 - Demonstrated LP or trader outcome improvements.
 - Moved the needle on core KPIs.
 Minimum qualifications 
 - 3+ years smart‑contract engineering, with 2+ years shipping production DeFi at protocol teams (DEX, lending, perps, bridges, market making infrastructure, oracles).
 - Deep Solidity and EVM internals; strong with Foundry, fuzzing, property tests; comfort reading/implementing community smart contracts.
 - Knowledge of the most common security pitfalls.
 - Deep and practical understanding of Uniswap v4 architecture (PoolManager, Hooks, singleton design, state scoping, callback surfaces).
 - Practical understanding of Uniswap v3 concentrated liquidity model.
 - Strong understanding of liquidity routing infrastructure - aggregators, routers, and solvers.
 - Demonstrated product sense in DeFi: able to reason about incentives, MEV, LP/trader UX, and distribution realities.
 - A portfolio of shipped, battle‑tested contracts and public design docs, posts, or talks.
 Nice‑to‑have signals 
 - Shipped a v4 hook on mainnet with end‑to‑end readiness - hands‑on learnings and production experience are desirable.
 - Emphasis on scalable and organized testing suites. Test-driven design practices.
 How the team works 
 - Product focused: Intentional about building for target markets instead of randomly throwing ideas. There is no one DEX design that fits all use cases, so markets are approached with different lenses - Ethereum volatile pairs, stable‑stable pairs, BTC‑fi pairs, RWAs and also chain dynamics (Arbitrum vs Base vs Mainnet vs Unichain).
 - Velocity with security as a feature: Focused on solving one problem at a time and shipping with high velocity, without compromising on security. Staged rollouts, clear escape hatches, no heroics.
 - Small, senior squads: Initiatives are led, not tickets.
 - Data‑anchored decisions: ship → measure → iterate.
 - Public goods stewardship: Like Ethereum core devs, the team acts as stewards of shared infrastructure. Primitives are designed with ecosystem adoption in mind, ensuring they are neutral, composable, and useful beyond just one chain.
 Application prompts (short and telling) 
 Please include two things with the application:
 1. A hook idea to ship in the next 12 weeks. Explain why and how this idea would be chosen: how the market opportunity is mapped, the target pair defined, trade segment, and reasoning through ecosystem router/aggregator integration.
    - Outline: state, which lifecycle callbacks would be used (beforeInitialize/beforeSwap/afterSwap/…), key invariants, and gas/MEV risks.
 2. A link to a deployed DeFi contract & Github from a previous project that facilitates valuable economic activity. What was the initial design, and how did it evolve as market‑share dynamics were observed?
    - While not all developers write multi-million dollar TVL contracts, DeFi insight, security, and learnings along the way are especially valued.
 Interview flow (what to expect) 
 - 30‑min intro: mandate & portfolio walkthrough.
 - Deep‑dive design exercise: scope a hook and discuss edge cases, tests, and rollout plan.
 - Live code review: read a small v4 hook and identify risks; write 2–3 properties to fuzz.
 - Security focused interview with Security collaborator.
 - Product/strategy chat with Growth: adoption plan, partners, and metrics.
 - Take home assignment: implement a hook involving flash accounting and provide a robust test suite.

 In pursuit of a more open and fair financial system, the client supports the growth, decentralization, and sustainability of the Uniswap community. Through grants, value is driven in five key focus areas: Protocol and Innovation, Developers, Governance, Research, and Security. The grant making approach is designed to maximize positive impact, bringing in new contributors to the community who focus on building new initiatives, committees, products, infrastructure, and more.  We are looking for a senior software developer who has made AI a structural part of how they build software — applying agentic systems, knowledge pipelines, and AI-connected tooling not as features, but as engineering fundamentals.
 This is not a role for someone who has added AI features to an app. We're looking for an experienced engineer who has restructured how software gets built — using AI agents to automate development tasks, MCPs to connect AI systems to real tools and data, and knowledge repositories to give AI systems reliable, domain-specific grounding. 
 Strong software architecture and system design are the baseline. AI tool mastery is the differentiator. This role sits at the intersection of both, and neither substitutes for the other.
 What You'll Do 
 Build Software Using AI as the Primary Instrument 
 Design, develop, and maintain production-grade SaaS applications using AI agents and tooling as first-class parts of your workflow, not bolt-ons. Use agentic systems to automate development tasks: scaffolding, refactoring, test generation, code review, documentation. Build and maintain MCP servers that connect AI systems to codebases, APIs, databases, and internal tools so AI assistants have reliable, scoped access to the context they need. Design and maintain knowledge repositories (vector databases, retrieval pipelines, embeddings) that give AI systems accurate, current, domain-specific grounding. Apply these tools across the full SDLC: from architecture drafting and requirements analysis through implementation, testing, and deployment.
 Architect Systems, Not Just Features

Reason through tradeoffs explicitly and document them so others can understand the reasoning, not just the outcome. Design for observability, reliability, and failure from the start.
